posts.title: Hello to everyone from Brazil
posts.text: Hello everyone in the Eurobricks community. My name is Pietro Perizzollo, In the past, I was a regular reader of the forum, following the creations that for us here in Brazil have always served as a source of inspiration. Although I’ve been visiting the site since 2011, I had never actually posted anything until now. I’d like to take this opportunity to share some things of my participation in the hobby in the community. The LEGO community here in Brazil has led to many friendships through events held across the country, and I’ve also had the chance to attend events in the U.S. and Denmark. I’m also involved with the AFOL community in Bolivia. I don’t have a large portfolio of MOCs, but for the moment I’d like to share two creations and made available on Rebrickable: https://rebrickable.com/users/firestorm226/mocs/ I like eveything made withs bricks but my main focus is lego cars

posts.title: [WIP] Jamestown: A Colonial Redcoat Capital
posts.text: Sharing a few more photos of the display. Here, a sentry guards the entry into town. The campfire behind him was part of the original encampment we build for the Redcoats so I wanted to make sure it made it into this display as well. A JTC Captain inspects the ring he just acquired on his latest voyage. He probably has a special someone in mind. I wonder if she will say yes? I really like the way this side of the display turned out. Working that old Cannon Cove and yellow sand into the newer style bricks was something I wasn't sure would work out aesthetically speaking, but I really think it came together nicely. It looks better in person, of course. I've said it before but taking pictures of Legos is surprisingly difficult. I'll share updates as I make them too. I still have a few roofs and buildings to put the finishing touches on for now, for example. And I need to populate the place a little more. The idea is for this to be a busy city, so I want it to look like one!

posts.title: [WIP] Jamestown: A Colonial Redcoat Capital
posts.text: You sort of read my mind. The initial build was to get it done. From here I'll study building techniques and ways to add the kind of detail you are describing. Chimneys are another detail on my list. I'll also try to add some interior detail, though I'll keep this to a minimum in most cases since you can't see inside most of the buildings. The roof windows was another one I really considered and likely will implement. Lovely thing about Lego. A display like this is never truly done. Another change I may make is replacing the trees with some newer trees to add height. I'm on the fence on this one because I do like the way these old vintage pine trees look.

posts.title: Kinebrick Studio
posts.text: Innovative initiative combining available libraries and technological capabilities with deep knowledge about the subject! You had me on board seeing GBC machines moving real time without much effort. A game changer in designing, visualising and validating moving parts for those who like to design digitally before building with real bricks. Still, design ideas with working mechanisms come from passionate designers, but this seems a great tool to facilitate the process from idea to final working build, and/or an educational way to visualize LEGO mechanics.

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Yup- I was hoping the Sanctum's reveal meant we'd see the whole wave, but I guess it's just this set for some reason. Hopefully the others will pop up soon. This is something that isn't appreciated enough, I think. We really are in a new golden age as far as lego marvel is concerned. Long gone are the days where everything is a spider-man set with a vehicle he doesn't need (not that those are 100% gone, but they also have their place for little kids)- the Mini-Modulars, Epic Moments sets, the shear breadth of what gets covered now. I don't think there was a single point in the theme before now where I'd have thought a character like Lasher (from obscurity) or F.R.I.D.A.Y. in Tony's corpse (exclusive to a TV-MA series) would be legitimate options for playsets. And 2027 is just pumping that to the max. I know it's not brought up here by anyone but me, but breaking into Rivals sets is big. Most of the main Doomsday designs we're missing are said to show up this year. We are finally getting the single most requested minifigure since the start of the theme. (Even if it's the raimi version). Ashnflash made a photoshop of Namor's head/hair on the iron man body and I 100% subscribe to the idea that this was intentionally done so you could also use it for Tony. If you look at the zombies in the show it actively looks more like Tony than Namor, there are some details missing for Namor. To be fair he did get turned into a zombie.

posts.title: Wet Winds - an RC windmill building operation
posts.text: Thanks for all your wonderful comments! One thing that didn't get emphasized in the video; my 3.5 kg crane is supported by six of these heavy duty caster wheels: [link to highres] The trouble with caster wheels in Lego is that the forces acting on the rotation axle cause a lot of friction. The 2x2 tiles with technic hole act as a support- this distributes the forces on the caster wheel, and acts as a rudimentary ballbearing. They allow reasonably low-friction movement- the noticably lighter tugboat has no trouble pushing and pulling the crane barge around.

posts.title: Kinebrick Studio
posts.text: Lately I have been working on a passion project that is starting to materialize into something I want to share with the community. I have always had a dream of a LEGO editor that was more geared (pun intended) towards the technical side of the hobby, I want simple tools to build linkages, threads, chains, shock absorbers and pneumatics. I also want i all to function in the editor. This is exactly what I have been building the last weeks. The editor is powered by the Kinebrick Engine, a deterministic engine for LEGO Technic: gears, motors, linkages and more. It can also be used to power games. I have made a small puzzle game with it that I will hopefully also release once it reaches a certain level. My motivation is many years in the GBC community trying to build advanced contraptions in software that was made for building MOCs and dioramas. So we needed something else. I have added a few videos to my channels and more will come. https://www.youtube.com/@fhareide Some highlights of what it can do: Build Opens real models: LDraw .ldr and .mpd files and BrickLink Studio .io files, tested up to 46,000 parts. It uses the full LDraw parts library. Technic-aware snapping: pins, axles and studs click into their connections. “Turn on pivot” and the swing tool rotate a part around the joint it sits on. Flexible parts: you route flexible axles, hoses, pneumatic tubes and strings by dragging their ends from hole to hole, and they follow live when you move the parts they’re attached to. Helpers: “Wrap a chain” around sprockets, stretch rubber bands, and use “Fit a shock absorber” to fit one between two pins. Fix-it tools: Overlap check flags parts placed on top of each other. Check placement finds parts sitting slightly off their connection and snaps them into place. Compare with… shows two versions of a model side by side in 3D: moved, added, removed and recoloured parts. Simulate Press play and it moves: add a real LEGO motor and battery box, and the gears mesh at the correct ratios, axles show their RPM, chains run and linkages swing. Real loads: motors slow down and stall under load, and you can switch between ideal speed and real motor behaviour. Linkages: 4-bar linkages, crank-sliders, universal joints with true Cardan motion, and Akiyuki-style GBC modules like the Hockey Stick Lift. Ball runs: Great Ball Contraption balls get lifted, rolled and dumped by the mechanism. It tells you why it’s stuck: jammed gear trains, binding linkages and motors that drive nothing show up under Problems. Clicking one highlights the culprit in red. Interference check: it drives the mechanism through its whole cycle and lists every collision, posing the model at each one. Range of motion: shows how far each part swings, turns or slides. Hoping that the first beta will be out very soon! Let me know if you have ideas or something I should get in.
